app.name: Bridge
app.tagline: We are not enemies. We are two people trying to get back to each other.
basement.answer_instruction: Answer with just one of the three words above — nothing more is required.
basement.instruction: Say your fear honestly, one at a time, out loud — a card can help you find the words. Your partner answers with only one of the three words below, then it's their turn. Up to 15 fears each; tap Done when you're finished.
basement.response.understand: I understand why it seemed that way
basement.why_it_helps: Why this helps: underneath the shouting is usually a frightened child, not a villain — naming the fear out loud lets your partner finally see that.

housemap.body: The task is simple: walk through every room of the house, one at a time, in the order shown. Each room asks one honest question — and only that kind of question, nothing else. When you've been through every room, you'll arrive together at the bridge, where you meet in the middle and reach out a hand to each other. If it gets overwhelming, you can close the app at any point — your progress is saved, and you can come back later, even this evening, to finish building the bridge.

privacy.full_text:
Last updated: this text ships with the app and should be re-dated whenever it changes.

Bridge is designed to work without a server. This policy describes exactly what the app does, matching its actual architecture — nothing here describes aspirational or future behavior.

WHAT BRIDGE COLLECTS

• Partner names, session data (intensity, state, cards played, token counts), and your Couple's Agreement are stored only in the app's local storage on your device. None of it is sent to us or to any third party.
• Voice snapshots (the optional 10-second recordings at the Bridge) are saved only as audio files on your device. They are never uploaded, synced, or shared — including with us.
• Bridge does not require an account, sign-in, or internet connection to work.
• Bridge does not use analytics, advertising SDKs, or third-party trackers.

WHAT BRIDGE DOES NOT DO

• We do not sell your data. There is no data to sell — it never leaves your device.
• We do not share your data with third parties, because we never receive it in the first place.

DELETING YOUR DATA

You can permanently delete a relationship profile — its tokens, session history, couple's agreement, and any voice notes — from Settings → Delete this relationship's data. Deleting the app itself also removes all of its local data, per standard iOS behavior.

CHILDREN

Bridge is not directed at children and is rated 12+ due to mature emotional themes.

CHANGES

If this policy changes, the updated text will ship with the app update and the "Last updated" line above will change accordingly.

CONTACT

Questions about this policy can be sent to the support address listed on Bridge's App Store page.

ritual.instruction: Say it together, however it fits you.
ritual.line_1: I'm sorry you were hurt in this.
ritual.title: Hold hands
room.basement.forbidden:
• No arguing with the other's fear
• No long defensive explanations before answering
room.basement.name: Basement
room.basement.question: Fears
room.hall.forbidden:
• No arguing
• No making excuses
• No correcting the other's account
room.hall.instruction: Take turns as a neutral witness. Describe only the facts you saw or heard — no blame, no interpretation. Example: “You raised your voice and left the room” — not “You always do this because you don't care.” Choose the event cards that match what you experienced.
room.hall.name: Hall
room.hall.question: What happened?
room.hall.why_it_helps: Why this helps: hearing your partner's own account, without blame, shows you the missing half of what happened.
room.kids_room.forbidden: • No arguing with the other's feelings
room.kids_room.instruction: This is self-reflection: which old wound got touched? A fear of being abandoned, of not being enough, of being controlled. Example: “This touches my fear of being left.” Your partner can't argue with it — it isn't about them, it's about what got triggered in you.
room.kids_room.name: Kids' Room
room.kids_room.question: What did this touch from my past?
room.kids_room.why_it_helps: Why this helps: naming the old wound lets your partner see someone hurting, not an enemy.
room.kitchen.instruction: Now talk together, freely — what would actually help avoid this next time? Real, doable ideas only.
room.kitchen.name: Kitchen
room.kitchen.question: What would help us avoid this?
room.kitchen.why_it_helps: Why this helps: turning the conflict into a shared plan is what keeps it from happening again.
room.living_room.forbidden:
• No arguing with the other's feelings
• No saying “you shouldn't feel that way”
room.living_room.instruction: This is subjective — say what YOU felt, emotionally and in your body. It may surprise your partner, and that's the point: hearing it out loud helps them see you're not being cruel, you're hurting. Example: “My chest went tight — I felt scared and alone.”
room.living_room.name: Living Room
room.living_room.question: What did you feel during this conflict?
room.living_room.why_it_helps: Why this helps: when you both feel like the villain to each other, saying the real feeling out loud — however it sounds — is what breaks that. Don't be afraid to say it as it is.
room.mode_caption.discussion: Dialogue allowed — talk it through together.
room.mode_caption.sequential: One partner speaks — the other only listens, no comments yet.
room.study.forbidden:
• No arguing with the other's interpretation
• No saying “that's not what I meant”
room.study.instruction: Say what the situation seemed to MEAN to you — even if it sounds exaggerated in hindsight. This shows how a mind can spiral into a story that isn't fully true, and helps your partner understand your reaction instead of just judging it. Example: “It felt like you don't love me anymore.”
room.study.name: Study
room.study.question: What did it mean to me?
room.study.why_it_helps: Why this helps: seeing how a thought can spiral shows your partner you're not being irrational — you're in pain.

Last updated: this text ships with the app and should be re-dated whenever it changes.

By using Bridge, you agree to these terms.

WHAT BRIDGE IS

Bridge is a guided communication tool for couples — a structured set of prompts, cards, and rituals meant to help two people talk through a conflict. It is not therapy, counseling, or any form of medical or mental health treatment, and it does not replace professional support. If you or your partner are experiencing abuse, crisis, or ongoing distress, please contact a licensed professional or a crisis line in your country (see Settings → Need help now?).

PURCHASES

Bridge's first full session is free. The full version is unlocked with a one-time, non-subscription in-app purchase, processed by Apple. You can restore a previous purchase on a new device from the paywall's Restore Purchases button. Refunds are handled by Apple under the App Store's standard refund policy — Bridge cannot issue refunds directly.

YOUR CONTENT

Anything you type or record in Bridge (names, cards, voice notes) stays on your device, as described in the Privacy Policy. You're responsible for what you and your partner choose to write, say, or record.

NO WARRANTY

Bridge is provided "as is." We don't guarantee it will resolve any particular conflict or improve any particular relationship — it's a tool, not a promise.

LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

To the fullest extent permitted by law, Bridge's developer is not liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from use of the app.

CHANGES

If these terms change, the updated text will ship with the app update and the "Last updated" line above will change accordingly.

CONTACT

Questions about these terms can be sent to the support address listed on Bridge's App Store page.
